verified_this_round.evidence: Reproduced both mutations against the exact fixture (comment header / #TODO / blank / real entry) by running the real check-coverage.sh. Baseline: exit 0, 'EXCLUDED:' printed. Mutation A (skip clause -> line.startswith('#') only, dropping 'not line'): the blank line reaches parts[0] and raises IndexError; gate exits 1 and prints a Traceback -- caught twice, by startsWith("0") and by doesNotContain("Traceback"). Mutation B (skip clause -> 'not line' only, dropping startswith('#')): '#TODO' parses as a single-token entry and the gate exits 1 with 'baselines/coverage.txt:2  "#TODO" is excluded with no reason' -- caught twice, by startsWith("0") and by doesNotContain("is excluded with no reason"). One fixture, both mutations, redundant assertions on each. Genuinely closed.

Reproduced four locator mutations. enumerate(open(BASELINE)) without start=1 -> 'coverage.txt:1' and malformed.append((0, parts[0])) -> 'coverage.txt:0' are both killed by contains("coverage.txt:2"). malformed.append((n, BASELINE)) and substituting BASELINE for name in the format args both print '"baselines/coverage.txt"' and are killed by contains("\"format\""); note both of these still satisfy the line-number assertion, so the two assertions are independently load-bearing rather than one covering for the other. The only surviving substitution is parts[0] -> line, which is behaviourally equivalent for every reachable input (a malformed entry is by definition a single token after strip). Genuinely closed.
